member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Chart.HidePlotZones
member.summary: Hides the plot content by clipping the draw-margin and crosshair zones to a zero-area rectangle. Used by every chart engine when the draw margin collapses (the reserved margins exceed the control), so the previous, now-invalid frame is not left painted at its old transform. A constructed (location, size) rectangle is NOT — Empty means "no clip / draw everywhere" — so even at the origin this reliably clips out all pixels. The legend, title and labels live in the NoClip zone and are intentionally untouched.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Chart.ResetPlotZoneClips
member.summary: Resets the plot zone clips back to (no clip). Engines that do not otherwise manage their clips (pie, polar, treemap, sankey) call this on a valid measure so a previous is undone and the plot becomes visible again. Engines that set real clips on every valid measure (cartesian via RegisterClipZones, geo map) restore themselves and don't need it.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreAxis`2.MeasureSeparatorAtValue(System.Double,System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{System.String,LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Helpers.AxisVisualSeprator},System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Helpers.AxisVisualSeprator},LiveChartsCore.AxisMeasureContext@)
member.summary: Per-separator-value body of the EnumerateSeparators loop. Looks up (or creates) the AxisVisualSeprator for the value, lazily initializes any visual shapes whose paint is configured but not yet rendered, attaches/detaches paints based on ShowSeparatorLines, drives all UpdateMode.Update transitions, and marks the separator as measured this frame so the cleanup pass knows to keep it.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreAxis`2.GetBandParityAnchor(System.Double,System.Double,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Double})
member.summary: Returns a stable ordinal for the cell that starts at the first separator, used to anchor the alternating-bands parity across pan. The default assumes evenly-stepped separators (the step quotient is the cell ordinal — stable while the tick step doesn't change; a re-tier legitimately reshuffles the bands). Axes that group their separators (e.g. a DateTimeAxis grouping time units) override this with an exact cell ordinal.

Falls back to the full draw margin when the engine hasn't assigned a rectangle yet — covers the single-series case where no partition is needed.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.EnsureVisualForNode(System.Object,LiveChartsCore.Drawing.LvcRectangle,LiveChartsCore.TreemapMeasureContext@)
member.summary: Ensures a visual exists for the given node. On first creation seeds the visual at the tile's center with zero size so the squarified position is reached via animation.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.UpdateVisualGeometry(`1,LiveChartsCore.Drawing.LvcRectangle,LiveChartsCore.TreemapMeasureContext@)
member.summary: Applies the squarified rectangle (minus padding) to the visual. The motion layer tweens to the new values automatically.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.CollapseRemovedVisual(`1)
member.summary: Collapses a removed tile to zero size at its center for a clean exit.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.InitializePaints(LiveChartsCore.TreemapChartEngine)
member.summary: Sets per-Z-index ordering on Fill / Stroke / DataLabelsPaint and registers them as drawable tasks on the canvas. Labels sit above tiles (PieSeriesDataLabelsBaseZIndex offset) and do not clip to the draw margin.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.ResolveValue(`0)
member.summary: Resolves a node's weight. Falls back to the sum of its descendants' resolved weights when the node has children and no explicit non-zero value of its own. When mappers are not configured but the node is a built-in , its members are used directly — covers the XAML path where source-generated wrappers instantiate the underlying series with an erased TModel that prevents the facade constructor's auto-wire from running. Memoized per measure pass (cleared at the top of and ) so deep hierarchies don't re-sum the same subtrees at every depth.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.ResolveChildren(`0)
member.summary: Resolves a node's children, with the same TreemapNode fallback as .

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.ResolveLabel(`0)
member.summary: Resolves a node's label, with the same TreemapNode fallback as .

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.EnsureChartPoint(`0,LiveChartsCore.Drawing.LvcRectangle,LiveChartsCore.TreemapMeasureContext@)
member.summary: Creates or refreshes the for a leaf — its HoverArea is set to the tile rectangle, Coordinate.PrimaryValue to the resolved weight, and DataSource to the user's node model so the tooltip formatter can access either via context or the typed point.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.CoreTreemapSeries`3.MeasureDataLabel(`0,LiveChartsCore.Drawing.LvcRectangle,LiveChartsCore.TreemapMeasureContext@)

member.summary: A sankey ribbon used in BipartiteArc layout — a closed Bezier band whose anchors are two chord endpoints on each arc (instead of vertical chords on rectangle edges, as assumes). Implements so each ribbon can carry its own tint while sharing a single Paint task.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.Drawing.BaseSankeyRibbonGeometry
member.summary: A sankey flow ribbon — a closed Bezier band connecting the right edge of a source node to the left edge of a target node. Six animatable endpoints (X + top-Y + bottom-Y for each end) drive the path; the platform-specific implementation builds two cubic curves with control points at the horizontal midpoint between source and target. Implements so each ribbon can carry its own tint (typically derived from its source node) while sharing a single Paint task.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Drawing.BaseSankeyRibbonGeometry.#ctor
member.summary: Initializes to the sentinel so the ribbon defaults to "use the shared paint color." Without this, the source-gen would default to default(LvcColor) = (0,0,0,0,IsEmpty=false), which the Draw's !Equals(Empty) check treats as a real (transparent black) override — and the ribbon renders invisible.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.GeoMapChart
member.summary: Defines a geo map chart.
member.remarks:
PHASE 1 SKETCH: inherits from so the map participates in the same lifecycle / throttler / pointer pipeline as Cartesian, Pie, Polar.
What this class no longer owns (delegated to base): - _updateThrottler, _panningThrottler and the Update / UpdateThrottlerUnlocked methods. - _pointerPosition, _isPointerIn, _isPointerDown, _isPanning, _pointerPanningPosition, _pointerPreviousPanningPosition (all base internals). - The custom Action<LvcPoint> pointer events; fires its own Action<Chart, LvcPoint> events. - Canvas (via base), the Load/Unload shells.
What stays geo-specific (overrides): - , , , family. - Land-based tooltip pipeline (own _tooltipThrottler — different semantics from ; unifying is Phase 2 work). - Viewport state (zoom, pan, rotation) and bounce/rotation animators.

member.summary: Projects (longitude, latitude) onto the chart's screen-space pixel coordinates using the projector built by the last pass. Returns null when the coordinate isn't visible — e.g. the back hemisphere on . The projection honors the current draw margin, title/legend reservations, and orthographic rotation; pair with for the inverse.

member.summary: Wraps a and positions it at a geographic (longitude, latitude) on a . member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Geo.IGeoMapView.MinLatitude
member.summary:
Gets or sets the minimum latitude (in degrees) clipped to the bottom edge of the rendered map. (the default) means the projection picks its own default — Mercator uses (-65°), cropping the sub-Antarctic empty band; Default uses
(-90°). Honored by Mercator and Default; ignores it (use instead).

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Geo.IGeoMapView.MaxLatitude
member.summary:
Gets or sets the maximum latitude (in degrees) clipped to the top edge of the rendered map. (the default) means the projection picks its own default — Mercator uses (85°), which already covers Greenland; Default uses
(90°). To render the classic full-earth Mercator including Antarctica, extend the bottom edge: set = -85. Honored by Mercator and Default; ignores it.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Geo.IGeoMapView.MinLongitude
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum longitude (in degrees) clipped to the left edge of the rendered map. (the default) means the projection picks its own default (-180° for both Mercator and Default). Honored by Mercator and Default; ignores it (use instead).

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Geo.IGeoMapView.MaxLongitude
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum longitude (in degrees) clipped to the right edge of the rendered map. (the default) means the projection picks its own default (180° for both Mercator and Default). Honored by Mercator and Default; ignores it.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Observers.CollectionDeepObserver
member.summary: A Class that tracks the event of a collection and, when item tracking applies (it can be disabled for element types that can never be tracked — see — and never applies to value-type items, whose subscription would attach to a temporary box), the event of each element in the collection.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Observers.CollectionDeepObserver.#ctor(System.Action,System.Action{System.Object},System.Action{System.Object})
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
member.param: An action that is called when the collection items or a property in an item in the collection change.
if specified, this action is called for each new item in the collection. This action is also called for each item when the collection is initialized.
if specified, this action is called each time an item is removed in the collection. This action is also called for each item when the collection is disposed.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Observers.CollectionDeepObserver.#ctor(System.Action,System.Action{System.Object},System.Action{System.Object},System.Boolean)
member.param: Whether items could need tracking — generic callers decide statically via . When false and no per-item callbacks are registered, the per-item walk is skipped entirely: it is O(N) and boxes every struct, which at large-data scale (a multi-million-point double[] or struct collection assigned to a series) measures in SECONDS of pure overhead per assignment.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Observers.CollectionDeepObserver.MayContainTrackableItems``1
member.summary:
Whether any instance of could ever need tracking:
A VALUE TYPE never can — even one implementing INPC: enumerating through the non-generic boxes each item, so the subscription would attach to a temporary box the collection does not hold (the handler can never fire) while the observer roots that box. Skipping is both faster and more correct.
A SEALED reference type that does not implement INPC has no INPC instances.
Anything else (an INPC type, an open hierarchy) may contain trackable items.
Evaluated on the statically-known type only — AOT/trimmer safe, no reflection over the collection instance.

member.summary:
Optionally returns an override that takes over drawing, bounds and hit-testing for the given (bypassing its per-point pipeline). Returns (the default) to let the series handle itself.
Consulted frequently — once per measure pass for rendering and bounds, and again on every pointer move/down for hit-testing, plus on series removal — and not cached by the engine. Implementations should make this cheap (e.g. a dictionary keyed by series) rather than allocating per call.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Providers.ChartEngine.GetAxisRenderOverride(LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Sketches.ICartesianAxis)
member.summary: Gets the render override for the given cartesian axis, if any. The override takes over how the axis lays out its separators and labels; the engine decides which axes are overridden — e.g. by the axis' concrete type and its own opt-in flags, like GroupTimeUnits on the DateTime axis (consulted while measuring; the axis caches the result by the visible range, so it re-runs on zoom/pan but is skipped while the range is unchanged). Return (the default) to let the axis lay itself out as usual. Consulted on every measure pass, so implementations should be cheap (e.g. a type check + flag read) rather than allocating per call.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.RenderingSettings
member.summary: LiveCharts rendering settings, this class is used to configure the rendering engine.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.RenderingSettings.UseGPU
member.summary: Indicates whether hardware acceleration is used, this will only work if the platform and device support it. This is ignored in Avalonia and Uno-Desktop because in those platforms the frame rate and rendering cadence is determined by them. Default is false, except on Blazor where the default is true (WebGL renders desktop-quality charts; raster mode is uglier and only worth opting into when WebGL is unavailable).

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.RenderingSettings.SetPlatformDefaultUseGPU(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets the default value for from a view-platform initializer. No-op if the consumer has already assigned explicitly, so user configuration always wins over platform defaults.

members.member: Indicates whether the rendering cadence should be aligned with the display refresh rate, GPU acceleration is required for this to work. This is ignored in Avalonia and Uno-Desktop because in those platforms the frame rate and rendering cadence is determined by them.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.RenderingSettings.LiveChartsRenderLoopFPS
member.summary: Defines the desired frames per second when using the LiveCharts render loop, this has no effect when is true and is true. Default is 60. This is ignored in Avalonia, the frame rate is determined by Avalonia itself.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.RenderingSettings.ShowFPS

member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum step, the step defines the interval between every separator in the axis, LiveCharts will calculate it automatically based on the chart data and the chart size size, if the calculated step is less than the then will be used as the axis step, default is 0.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Sketches.IPlane.ForceStepToMin
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the axis should use the as the actual step of the axis, if true, the library will not calculate the step of the axis automatically, instead it will use the value in the property. Be careful when setting this property to true, it might cause performance issues if the step is too small for the current data in the chart. Default value is false.

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.Kernel.Sketches.IPlane.MinSeparators
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum number of separators (gridlines/labels) the axis should display when the step is calculated automatically. The library snaps the auto-step up to a nice number (1, 2, 5, 10 × magnitude), and on small charts that snap can leave too few separators visible; this property forces the auto-step to subdivide further until at least this many separators fit in the visible range. Set to 0 to disable. Ignored when is true. Default is 3.

member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum value visible in the axis, any point less than this value will be hidden, set it to null (or double.NaN) to use a value based on the smaller value in the chart.

member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum value visible in the axis, any point greater than this value will be hidden, set it null (or double.NaN) to use a value based on the greater value in the chart.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout
member.summary:
d3-sankey layout (Bostock 2012 / Riehmann 2005). Assigns each node a column based on longest-path depth, distributes nodes vertically within each column with iterative sweep-relaxation to minimize ribbon crossings, then computes per-link Y bands at each end.
Output is consumed by ; the algorithm itself is pure-functional (no chart references) so it can be snapshot-tested independently and reused if a second sankey-shaped series family ever appears.
Assumes a DAG. Self-loops are silently dropped. Cycles throw — detecting + breaking them automatically is out of scope for v1 (a real sankey diagram with cycles is almost always a data bug).

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.NodeBox.Value
member.summary: Layout-computed node value (max of incoming + outgoing weight sums).

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.ArcResult`1
member.summary: Result of — same shape as but with arc-segment node boxes and chord ribbon endpoints.

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.ArcNodeBox
member.summary: Per-node arc placement: annular sector centered at (CenterX, CenterY), from InnerRadius to OuterRadius, drawn clockwise from StartAngle for SweepAngle degrees (Skia convention).

member.name: P:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.ArcNodeBox.Value
member.summary: Layout-computed node value (max of incoming + outgoing weight sums).

member.name: T:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.ChordRibbonBox`1
member.summary: Per-link chord placement: 4 cartesian endpoints on inner-arc chords (two per node, in band order) plus the chart center used as the cubic-Bezier control attractor.

member.name: M:LiveChartsCore.SankeyLayout.ComputeBipartiteArc``1(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{``0},System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{LiveChartsCore.Defaults.SankeyLink{``0}},LiveChartsCore.Drawing.LvcRectangle,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
BipartiteArc layout: every node lies on one of two arcs (source nodes on a left arc centered at 180°, target nodes on a right arc centered at 0°), with ribbons curving through the chart center as cubic Beziers with control point at center. Returns angular node spans + the four chord endpoints per ribbon, all in cartesian coordinates derived from the inner radius of each node's arc segment.
Throws if the graph has more than two depth columns — caller is responsible for catching upstream and surfacing a clear API error.
Lays out one column's nodes on its arc — proportional sweeps from the column's value sum, separated by angularPadDeg.
